elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 13.4.1: "provided that AbbVie may make such an assignment without Harpoon's consent to its Affiliate..." — AbbVie (Customer) retains the affiliate carve-out from the mutual consent requirement, and "Affiliate" is a defined term (1.16).

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered 13.4.1: "...or to a successor, whether in a merger, sale of stock, sale of assets or any other transaction, of the business to which this Agreement relates" — covers merger, stock/asset acquisition and any other transaction in the relevant business, without Harpoon's consent.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The no-consent exception was narrowed from "either Party ... without the other Party's consent" to "AbbVie ... without Harpoon's consent," so Harpoon remains bound by the opening prohibition ("Without the prior written consent of the other Party ... neither Party shall sell, transfer, assign ... this Agreement"), with attempted assignments "void and of no effect."

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Retained opening words of 13.4.1: "such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed" — already-met existing language, correctly left untouched.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "and in no event shall Harpoon assign this Agreement to a Competitor" — an absolute, unconditional bar directed only at Harpoon; note the definitional caveat in the reasons below.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: No provision in the cited or rendered text confers a Harpoon termination or re-pricing right on an AbbVie change of control; Section 12.3 (quoted in the mapping) is AbbVie's own for-convenience termination right and is not evidence for this element, but the element is satisfied by the absence of any AbbVie-CoC trigger in Article 12/13.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: After the edit, only AbbVie may assign to a successor without consent; Harpoon's successor assignments now require AbbVie's prior written consent, so the mutual successor right the fallback contemplates is absent.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: 13.4.1 as rendered imposes no notice obligation on a permitted successor or Affiliate assignment; the only mechanics retained are continuing responsibility for Affiliate performance and assumption by the assignee.

A retained no-consent, non-successor exception survives (AbbVie may assign to "its Affiliate" without Harpoon's consent), which under the rule boundary defeats a general "other assignments require consent" formulation.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed" is retained in the opening sentence of 13.4.1.

reasons: Preferred level is complete on the operative text: Customer keeps the Affiliate and merger/stock/asset successor carve-out, Harpoon's mirror carve-out is removed so Harpoon needs AbbVie's consent, the existing reasonableness standard is retained, an absolute Harpoon-to-Competitor bar is added, and no clause gives Harpoon a termination right on an AbbVie change of control. Fallback is not met (no mutual successor right, no notice mechanic, retained AbbVie Affiliate no-consent exception), but that is irrelevant because the higher level is complete.

Definitional gap to close: the inserted bar uses capitalized "Competitor," which does not appear among the resolved Article 1 definitions. If the Agreement does not define "Competitor," add a definition (or replace with lower-case descriptive language, e.g. "any Third Party that, directly or through its Affiliates, develops or commercialises a product competitive with the products to which this Agreement relates") so the prohibition does not turn on an undefined term.

Minimality holds: the only changes are (i) narrowing "either Party ... the other Party's consent" to "AbbVie ... Harpoon's consent" — necessary to reach "Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent" — and (ii) the competitor bar required by element 5. The reasonableness standard, Affiliate-responsibility sentence, void-assignment sentence, binding-effect sentence, assumption sentence and the Harpoon-successor payment run-with sentence are all preserved verbatim; no survival tails, notice procedures or extra requirements were added.

Intent preserved: the retained sentence "With respect to an assignment to an Affiliate, the assigning Party shall remain responsible..." still operates sensibly (Harpoon may still assign to an Affiliate with consent), and the retained references to "successor or permitted assignee of Harpoon" remain coherent because Harpoon assignments are now permitted only with consent. No dangling cross-reference or contradictory retained sentence was created.

Drafting note for the mapping, not the text: the "already_met" quote offered for the change-of-control element (Section 12.3) is AbbVie's own convenience-termination right and does not evidence the absence of a Harpoon CoC trigger; cite Article 12's exhaustive Harpoon termination grounds (breach/insolvency) and Section 13.2 instead.
